Which neighborhoods need the van most?.answer: The four stops: 2026-11-07: Tract 120, need 0.41, ~106,189 residents within reach; 2026-11-14: Tract 82.03, need 0.35, ~37,565 residents within reach; 2026-11-21: Tract 116.34, need 0.32, ~72,694 residents within reach; 2026-11-28: Tract 116.47, need 0.36, ~40,193 residents within reach. Each is placed so its 4 km catchment covers as many high-need residents as possible. Prevalence figures are CDC PLACES model estimates, not counts.

Is respiratory illness rising in this ne.answer: I can't tell you that about a neighborhood, and neither can any public dataset we have. Respiratory emergency-visit data covers the whole four-county Health Service Area (Fulton, DeKalb, Clayton and Gwinnett), not a tract. Flu and COVID numbers are only reported for the whole Clayton, DeKalb, Fulton, Gwinnett area, not for your neighborhood. The latest numbers we have are from 2024-09-28. The plan gives it no weight.

Who does this plan reach?.answer: The four catchments reach about 263,815 of 1,051,550 residents. Black 44.2% vs 43.1% county-wide; Hispanic or Latino 8.5% vs 7.2% county-wide; Asian 11.0% vs 7.3% county-wide; White 33.0% vs 39.3% county-wide. No group falls below the 0.80 parity floor. This comparison is auditor-only: the planner never saw race or ethnicity.
